hints: Count squares by their bottom-right corner.
For one letter, find the largest square ending at each cell that does not contain it.
A square contains every letter exactly when it is larger than each letter-free square at that corner.
analogy: A square must grow past the largest missing-letter region before it has collected every required letter.
example: In the 2 by 2 grid AB/BA with letters A and B, all four single cells fail and the whole grid works, giving 1.
algorithm: For each letter in turn, compute a standard maximal-square DP on cells that are not that letter: dp[r,c] is zero on that letter and otherwise one plus the minimum of the top, left and top-left DP values. For each cell store the maximum of these dp values over all letters. If that maximum is M, there are min(r,c)-M valid squares ending there using one-based coordinates. Sum these counts. Only two DP rows are needed per letter; store the maximum for each cell.
correctness: For a fixed corner and letter, letter-free squares are nested and have every size up to the computed maximum. A square contains every letter exactly when its size exceeds all these maxima. Every square has exactly one bottom-right corner, so adding the number of valid sizes at each corner counts each once.
complexity: For an n by n grid with k letters, time is O(k n^2), and extra space is O(n^2) for the maxima plus O(n) for rolling DP rows.
